attempts.reason:
A high-effort review of PR #317 found 15 defects. `npm run lint` and both store suites are green
(72/72) — this is not a broken PR, it is an incomplete one. Five were reproduced with standalone
probes against the branch; I re-confirmed the first two by reading the code.

**Read this part first.** Three of the five are the same mistake: *you fixed the instance and left the
class.*

- You added `ATTEMPT_IDENTITY` so an attempt's identity comes from its position in the tree, never
  from inside the record — then left `collection()` (sqlite.js:735) preferring `rec.id` over the map
  key for cards. Its own comment says "The key *is* the id" and the line below it does the opposite.
- You made `_land` carry foreign paths across — then wrote `isOwned()` (git.js:842) to claim the whole
  `cards/`+`runs/` *prefixes*, so `cards/README.md` is still deleted. `_parseFiles` only ever
  recognises `cards/<digits>.json`; `isOwned` must match that pattern, not the directory.
- You fixed `Number(x) || fallback` in `nextId` and named it in the PR body — then shipped
  `Number(keep) || EVENT_RETENTION` in `trimEvents` (sqlite.js:692), where `{keep: 0}` from `hkb gc`
  silently keeps 50 000 rows.

So for every fix below, ask what else in these two files has the same shape, and fix that too.

## Must fix — reproduced, and A6 (#294) would inherit each one

1. **`load()` deletes every live lock when the tree omits `cards`** (sqlite.js:492).
   `DELETE FROM locks WHERE task_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM tasks) OR ...` — SQL's `NOT IN (empty set)`
   is true for every row, and `collection(undefined)` returns `[]` while `DELETE FROM tasks` has
   already run. The partial-tree shape is one your sibling `board` branch (line 427) explicitly
   supports. Repro: load a tree with card 1, `claim(1, 1)`, then `load({tip: 'bbb'})` → `locks_dropped: 1`,
   `listLocks()` empty, and the running worker's next `heartbeat(1, 1, token)` returns `lost` — exit 3,
   card handed back to the next tick. That is precisely the outcome this method's doc says the split
   exists to prevent. Reconcile only against a tree that actually carried cards.

2. **A card's identity comes from inside the record** (sqlite.js:735). `cards/7.json` carrying
   `"id": 3` after a hand edit or a bad merge indexes as card 3 titled 'seven'; `getTaskRow(7)` is
   null, `listTaskRows()` reports 3, and `claim(7, k)`'s `WHERE id = 7` matches nothing — card 7 is on
   the branch and invisible to every index read. When the colliding card does exist, the duplicate
   guard fires but names the wrong file. Take the id from the key, as you already do for runs.

3. **`gitCommonDir()` bypasses `runGit`** (board.js:904), so it never unsets `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`
   — and it is now the sole decider of where the index and the board root live. With
   `GIT_DIR=/tmp/theirs/.git` exported, `storeGitDir({root: '/tmp/mine'})` answers `/tmp/theirs/.git`,
   so the index becomes `/tmp/theirs/.git/hkb/index.db`. `runGit`'s own `GIT_UNSET` comment
   (board.js:225) names this exact hazard — "hkb's own Stop hook runs inside git sometimes" — and this
   PR added the one git spawn that skips it.

4. **`isOwned()` claims directory prefixes** (git.js:842) — see above. Also breaks the no-op guard:
   `sameTree`'s `had` counts `cards/README.md`, `want` never does, so every "nothing changed" write on
   such a board lands a commit that deletes it.

5. **`commit()` asserts a writable ref before the no-op check** (git.js:338), so a verb that decides
   nothing now throws exit 2 on a read-only clone where it previously returned `{changed: false}`
   without touching a ref. `setStatus` to the status a card already has, or `addLabels(task, [])`, both
   hard-fail on a clone. A reconcile pass that re-asserts current state is exactly what your `_patch`
   fix was meant to make free. Order the no-op check first.

## Also fix

6. **`closeTask()` re-stamps `closed_at` before `_patch` can compare** (git.js:653), so closing an
   already-closed card still lands a commit — a hole in the invariant `_patch`'s early return was added
   to establish. Your new test covers setStatus/setAgent/addLabels/removeLabel/updateBody/removeBlockedBy
   but not closeTask. Same shape: `addLabels(task, [])` on a card whose stored `labels` is unsorted
   commits, because `applyLabels` re-sorts unconditionally.
7. **`trimEvents({keep: 0})`** (sqlite.js:692) — the falsy-zero above. Use
   `Number.isInteger(k) && k >= 0 ? k : EVENT_RETENTION`, the form you used in `nextId`.
8. **`_absentRefMessage` over-asserts** (git.js:384). `classifyRefWrite` returns 'absent' for git's
   "unable to resolve reference", which is also what git says when the local ref is deleted between
   `readTree()` and the CAS (a concurrent `git branch -D kb-board`, `hkb down` racing a verb). The
   message then prescribes `git branch kb-board origin/kb-board`, which itself fails with "not a valid
   object name" when there is no remote-tracking ref. Reach that message only after confirming
   `_tip().local === false`; otherwise say the ref went away under the write.
9. **`load()` writes `board.slug` unconditionally** (sqlite.js:431), so a tree carrying a different
   slug silently repurposes an index `assertSameBoard` just cleared — the two-boards-in-one-repo bug
   moved from open time to load time.
10. **`locate()` gates its fallback on a strict `ctx === null`** (sqlite.js:304), so
    `openIndex(undefined, {file})` shells out to `storeRoot()` against `process.cwd()`. `index.root()`
    and `wake()`'s `readPidFile` then look in a different directory than the index lives in, and
    `wake()` swallows the miss and returns false — the dispatcher is never nudged. `const git` on line
    305 is also computed and discarded whenever `file` is given.
11. **`gitSays` widened github.js's loud-line regex with `warning`** (github.js:627). A
    `--force-with-lease` push printing `warning: redirecting to https://…` before `! [rejected] …
    (stale info)` now reports the warning plus the rejection instead of the rejection plus its reason —
    the two lines a human reads when a heartbeat returns `unavailable`. The consolidation is right; the
    merged regex should have been the union's *ranking*, not its membership.
12. **`readTree()` decodes every foreign blob as UTF-8** (git.js:278) and `_snap` then pins those
    strings for the process lifetime, though `_land` and `sameTree` only ever read `{sha, mode}` for
    non-owned paths. Restrict the `cat-file --batch` input to owned paths.
13. **`INSERT OR REPLACE INTO tasks` is dead code** (sqlite.js:439) — `DELETE FROM tasks` ran at 418
    and the `seen` guard throws three lines below. It says "a duplicate is fine" exactly where the
    guard says it is an error. Plain `INSERT`.
14. **`GIT_ENV` is exported and used nowhere outside board.js** (board.js:216) — the
    exported-and-unused pattern you removed for `DURABLE_METHODS`. Make it module-private.

## One judgment call, not a defect

15. CLAUDE.md says pure logic goes in `src/model.js` with a test in `test/`. `gitSays`,
    `normalizeCardGrants`, `classifyRefWrite`, `nextId`, `isOwned` and `slugFile` are all pure and all
    live in board.js or the drivers, reachable only through integration tests against temp repos.
    `classifyRefWrite`'s two measured git messages in particular are a table a model.js unit test would
    pin without a temp repo. Move what moves cleanly; if you judge any of them better placed where they
    are, say so on the card in one line rather than moving it.

## Done when

- [ ] Every item fixed, or one line on the card saying why not.
- [ ] A test for each of 1–8 — all were reproduced, so all are pinnable. Item 1 needs a partial-tree
      load with a live lock; item 5 needs a read-only clone.
- [ ] The "same mistake elsewhere" sweep above actually done, not just the listed instances.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green.

attempts.reason:
Round 3. Good round — you engaged with the headline rather than the list, generalized each fix
(`repoRoot` alongside `gitCommonDir`, `events({limit:0})` alongside `trimEvents`, `CARD_FILE`/`RUN_FILE`
shared so the parser and the ownership test cannot drift), reported your own mid-flight error, and
pushed back on item 15 with an argument instead of complying. Item 15 is accepted as you argued it:
`classifyRefWrite`, `isOwned` and `gitSays` stay where they are, exported and unit-tested. CI is green
on `dcc38b67`, so your last residual risk is closed.

A second high-effort review found 15 more. Most are the next layer down. Two are not.

**Read this first — one of your round-2 fixes did not land, and its test hides that.**

Item 5 last round was "`commit()` asks the no-op question before asserting a writable ref." You moved the
`sameTree` check above `_assertWritableRef` — but `_assertOwner` (git.js:345) still runs *before both*.
So on an actual clone the verb still throws exit 2, and the thing the fix was for — a reconcile pass
that re-asserts current state costing nothing on a clone — still hard-fails. The test passes only
because it constructs the tier with `{host: 'test-host'}`, the host that owns the board: **the one
configuration a real clone never has.** A test built to pass is worse than the bug, because it spends
the next reviewer's trust. Fix the order, and rewrite that test so the clone's host differs from
`board.host` — which is the whole scenario.

## Must fix

1. **`load()` clobbers a live attempt and then deletes its lock** (sqlite.js:508) — reproduced, and it is
   the same family as last round's item 1. A closed attempt off the branch overwrites the open index row
   via `INSERT OR REPLACE`, wiping `pid`/`job`/`wt`; the lock sweep then removes that card's lock, and the
   running worker's next heartbeat returns `lost` (exit 3). Your `if (!a || !a.ended_at) continue` guard
   inspects only the *tree's* row, never the index's, so the comment two lines above it — "an open one is
   this host's… writing it from the tree would clobber the pid the loop is watching" — is not enforced by
   anything. Repro: `claim(1,3)`, `setAttempt(1,3,{pid:4242,job:'j1',wt:'/tmp/wt'})`, then `load()` with
   `runs = Map{1:{attempts:[{attempt:3, ended_at:'e', outcome:'done'}]}}`. This is the real `hkb finish`
   window: the attempt is written closed to the branch before `release()` runs, and any tick reloading on
   the moved tip lands in it.

2. **`_assertOwner` before the no-op check** (git.js:345) — above.

3. **A foreign path containing a newline or tab corrupts the whole `update-index --index-info` payload**
   (git.js:488). Git permits both in path names and `ls-tree -z` hands them back raw — which is why you
   use `-z`. Before this PR only the tier's own three name patterns reached that line, so it was
   unreachable; carrying every foreign entry verbatim is what made it reachable. `update-index -z
   --index-info` with NUL-terminated records is the shape that survives it.

## Also fix

4. **`readSchemaVersion` swallows every error** (sqlite.js:248), so a transient `SQLITE_BUSY` reads as
   "no schema version" and the user is told to `rm` a database that is current and healthy — from
   `openIndexReadOnly` (`hkb serve`), the one connection not allowed to repair anything. Catch only the
   missing-`meta`-table case the comment names; let everything else propagate.
5. **`load()` is strict about `cards` and `runs` and still silently tolerant of a malformed `board`**
   (sqlite.js:463). `load({tip, board: 'default', ...})` — the slug where the document goes — moves
   `tip_sha`, leaves host/paused_at/paused_by/settings untouched, and reports success. Your own thesis
   applied to two of three collections. `collection()`'s `throw usage(...)` is what `board` needs.
6. **`slugFile` is not injective** (sqlite.js:101): `a/b` and `a-b` both become `index.a-b.db`, as do
   `Alpha`/`alpha` on macOS and Windows, and anything past 64 chars shares a prefix. Worse, the collision
   error tells the operator to `hkb --board a/b`, which resolves to the same file — advice that does
   nothing. Hash the slug into the name and the collision stops existing.
7. **`need()` (git.js:957) and `badRecord()` (sqlite.js) still hardcode `kb-board`** after every in-class
   message moved to `this.branch`. A tier on `refs/heads/kb-board-staging` tells the operator to run
   `git show kb-board:cards/7.json`. The constructor takes `ref` precisely so the name is not fixed;
   half the error surface honours it and half does not.
8. **The `UPDATE board SET slug` sits outside the try/catch that closes the connection** (sqlite.js:281),
   so a busy-timeout throw there leaks an open `DatabaseSync` plus its WAL/shm handles — the exact leak
   the rest of the function is wrapped to avoid, and the one the test file's new OPEN registry exists to
   prevent on Windows.
9. **`indexDir`/`indexFile` changed meaning without changing name or arity** (sqlite.js:98) — they take
   the common git dir where they took the repo root. `indexDir`'s own doc still says it is "for `hkb
   doctor` and `hkb init`'s ignore list", callers that land in a later node, and every *other* path helper
   in board.js (`kanbanDir`, `logsDir`, `pidFile`) takes a root. Whoever writes those reaches for
   `indexDir(ctx.root)` and silently gets `<root>/hkb`. Rename it (`indexDirIn(gitDir)`) or assert the
   argument is a git dir.
10. **`listTaskRows` builds the whole-board blocker map even for a filtered query** (sqlite.js:571), so a
    narrow `{status}` read — the dispatcher's hot path — is now slower than the N+1 it replaced: 500 link
    rows grouped to return 2 cards, where the old code did 2 indexed lookups. Restrict the grouping to
    `blocked_id IN (...)`, or build it lazily. Value 3 is performance; this is the one call that runs
    every tick.
11. **`cloneTree` structuredClones every card and run on each `readTree()`** (git.js:899), so `getTask(n)`
    on a 500-card board deep-clones 1000 records to return one, twice per verb. The memo traded 3 git
    spawns for an O(board) clone — still a win, but the read accessors only need per-record copies of what
    they return; only `commit()`'s mutation path needs the whole tree.
12. **`wake()` now shells out** (sqlite.js:748). Going through `readPidFile` was right, but it calls
    `readBtimeSec` unconditionally — `sysctl -n kern.boottime` on darwin — so every store write that
    nudges the loop forks a process, in a module that documents and tests "nothing here shells out". The
    guard test only greps this file's source, so it cannot see a spawn arriving through an import. Keep
    the staleness check; hoist or per-process-cache the boot instant.
13. **The GitHub driver's `listNotes` still drops any comment that *contains* the marker**
    (github.js:799) — the exact defect you fixed on the git tier, so the two drivers now disagree about
    what a note is. git.js:787 asserts "The GitHub store filters its comments with `startsWith` for the
    same reason", which is true of `latestResult` and not of `listNotes`. Fix it and add the case to
    `test/store.test.js`, since the conformance suite not covering a note that quotes a marker is why
    this diverged unseen.
14. **The `storeGitDir` test compares a non-canonical path against a realpath'd expectation**
    (test/store-sqlite.test.js:878) — the two assertions above it realpath both sides, this one only the
    expectation. Green on Linux, red anywhere tmpdir is a symlink.
15. **`docs/wiki/concepts/tool-grant-ceiling.md:43`** still says `normalizeCardGrants(kb)` is "in
    `src/store/github.js`", which this PR reduced to a re-export shim. It was already STALE for unrelated
    drift, so wiki-check gives no signal — but AGENTS.md asks for the page a change touches, and #318
    covers the rest of the backlog, not this.

## Done when

- [ ] Every item fixed, or one line on the card arguing why not — as you did for item 15, which worked.
- [ ] A test for 1, 2 and 3. Item 2's test must use a host that differs from `board.host`.
- [ ] The same sweep as last round: for each fix, what else has this shape?
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green.

   via `INSERT OR REPLACE`, wiping `pid`/`job`/`wt`; the lock sweep then removes that card's lock, and the
   running worker's next heartbeat returns `lost` (exit 3). Your `if (!a || !a.ended_at) continue` guard
   inspects only the *tree's* row, never the index's, so the comment two lines above it — "an open one is

   window: the attempt is written closed to the branch before `release()` runs, and any tick reloading on
   the moved tip lands in it.

2. **`_assertOwner` before the no-op check** (git.js:345) — above.

3. **A foreign path containing a newline or tab corrupts the whole `update-index --index-info` payload**

   use `-z`. Before this PR only the tier's own three name patterns reached that line, so it was
   unreachable; carrying every foreign entry verbatim is what made it reachable. `update-index -z
   --index-info` with NUL-terminated records is the shape that survives it.

## Also fix

4. **`readSchemaVersion` swallows every error** (sqlite.js:248), so a transient `SQLITE_BUSY` reads as
   "no schema version" and the user is told to `rm` a database that is current and healthy — from
   `openIndexReadOnly` (`hkb serve`), the one connection not allowed to repair anything. Catch only the
   missing-`meta`-table case the comment names; let everything else propagate.
5. **`load()` is strict about `cards` and `runs` and still silently tolerant of a malformed `board`**
   (sqlite.js:463). `load({tip, board: 'default', ...})` — the slug where the document goes — moves
   `tip_sha`, leaves host/paused_at/paused_by/settings untouched, and reports success. Your own thesis
   applied to two of three collections. `collection()`'s `throw usage(...)` is what `board` needs.
6. **`slugFile` is not injective** (sqlite.js:101): `a/b` and `a-b` both become `index.a-b.db`, as do
   `Alpha`/`alpha` on macOS and Windows, and anything past 64 chars shares a prefix. Worse, the collision
   error tells the operator to `hkb --board a/b`, which resolves to the same file — advice that does
   nothing. Hash the slug into the name and the collision stops existing.
7. **`need()` (git.js:957) and `badRecord()` (sqlite.js) still hardcode `kb-board`** after every in-class
   message moved to `this.branch`. A tier on `refs/heads/kb-board-staging` tells the operator to run
   `git show kb-board:cards/7.json`. The constructor takes `ref` precisely so the name is not fixed;
   half the error surface honours it and half does not.
8. **The `UPDATE board SET slug` sits outside the try/catch that closes the connection** (sqlite.js:281),
   so a busy-timeout throw there leaks an open `DatabaseSync` plus its WAL/shm handles — the exact leak

9. **`indexDir`/`indexFile` changed meaning without changing name or arity** (sqlite.js:98) — they take

   `indexDir(ctx.root)` and silently gets `<root>/hkb`. Rename it (`indexDirIn(gitDir)`) or assert the
   argument is a git dir.
10. **`listTaskRows` builds the whole-board blocker map even for a filtered query** (sqlite.js:571), so a
    narrow `{status}` read — the dispatcher's hot path — is now slower than the N+1 it replaced: 500 link

    every tick.
11. **`cloneTree` structuredClones every card and run on each `readTree()`** (git.js:899), so `getTask(n)`

12. **`wake()` now shells out** (sqlite.js:748). Going through `readPidFile` was right, but it calls

13. **The GitHub driver's `listNotes` still drops any comment that *contains* the marker**

14. **The `storeGitDir` test compares a non-canonical path against a realpath'd expectation**

15. **`docs/wiki/concepts/tool-grant-ceiling.md:43`** still says `normalizeCardGrants(kb)` is "in
